causal_research.bug_semantics: During ZIP extraction, a local attacker able to mutate the extraction directory can replace an already-validated parent directory with a symlink before OpenClaw opens the destination pathname. The later pathname-based write follows the rebound parent and can create or truncate a file outside the extraction root with the OpenClaw process's privileges; leaf-only O_NOFOLLOW protection does not bind mutable parent traversal to the checked directory identity.

That check/use separation created the parent-symlink TOCTOU window at inception; later streaming and partial symlink-hardening changes retained the same mutable-parent pathname resolution and are not origins.

causal_research.bug_semantics: The Zalo webhook router matched a registered route using the normalized URL pathname, but unauthenticated failure accounting used the raw req.url, including its query string, as part of the key in a process-global Map with no maximum size or expiry. An attacker could repeatedly POST to the same reachable valid webhook path with an invalid or missing secret while varying ?nonce=..., causing every 401 to create and retain a distinct webhookStatusCounters entry and eventually exert memory pressure or trigger OOM. The similarly raw-URL-keyed rate-limit map was also unbounded, although that path ran only after successful target authentication; the unauthenticated advisory path is the 401 status-counter insertion.
causal_research.flaw_origin: Commit a23e0d5140e5126f5055a46824cae4ba0a097ba3 added Zalo webhook ingress hardening, including anomaly accounting and rate limiting. In extensions/zalo/src/monitor.ts it introduced webhookStatusCounters as an unbounded Map, recordWebhookStatus() as an unconditional insertion for security error statuses, and calls that passed req.url for pre-authentication 401 responses. This composed a normalized route match with attacker-controlled raw-URL keying and unbounded retention; later commit 453664f09d0911cc1829d22c63f664f0ad2c8c10 only moved the already-vulnerable logic into monitor.webhook.ts.

causal_research.bug_semantics: A tenant able to create or update Fission Function or Environment CRDs could request SYS_TIME in securityContext.capabilities.add on a tenant-controlled container or init container. The v1.24.0 admission validator and executor merge sanitizer used a fixed denylist containing only SYS_ADMIN, NET_ADMIN, SYS_PTRACE, SYS_MODULE, DAC_READ_SEARCH, and DAC_OVERRIDE, so SYS_TIME passed both layers and reached the resulting pod. Without restrictive Pod Security Admission on the function-pod namespace, CAP_SYS_TIME permits clock_settime(CLOCK_REALTIME) against the node-wide, non-time-namespaced real-time clock, corrupting wall-clock-dependent state for co-tenants. The separate OCI-default-capability concern was not fully addressed by this advisory's fix.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An authenticated user able to create and run workflows could supply the Git node with a staged working repository whose configured push remote was another attacker-controlled local repository. For push and pushTags, vulnerable releases left Git's file transport enabled, causing local git-receive-pack to run receive-side hooks in the target repository as the n8n process. Setting core.hooksPath=/dev/null on the initiating repository did not suppress hooks in that local receive target. The fix validates configured remotes and removes file from GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL for write operations when hooks are disabled.
causal_research.flaw_origin: The original Git node accepted a workflow-selected baseDirectory, constructed simple-git for that repository, and exposed git.push() without restricting repository-controlled local remote targets or Git's file transport. That original trust-boundary crossing, rather than a later move, import, refactor, or aggregate landing, is the flaw origin.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Repo.clone() and Repo.clone_from() converted caller-supplied separate_git_dir/separate-git-dir input into git clone --separate-git-dir=<path> and executed it while allow_unsafe_options remained false. Because --separate-git-dir redirects the complete Git metadata directory, an attacker whose input is forwarded as a clone option can make Git create repository metadata outside the intended clone destination; the clone safety denylist omitted this option and therefore raised no UnsafeOptionError.

The contemporaneous command wrapper rendered separate_git_dir as --separate-git-dir=<value>, so this was the first affected public clone API and the first commit whose default clone path could honor an attacker-controlled external metadata directory. Later commit b425301ad16f265157abdaf47f7af1c1ea879068 added clone_from() on the same _clone path, and later safety-denylist commits e6108c7997f5c8f7361b982959518e982b973230 and 5c59e0d63da6180db8a0b349f0ad36fef42aceed preserved the original flaw by omitting --separate-git-dir.

causal_research.bug_semantics: PluginImportGuard.restore_hidden_modules() restored saved entries, cleared self.hidden_modules, and only then evaluated len(self.hidden_modules), so every restoration audit message reported zero regardless of the number restored. In setup, hide_dangerous_modules() deleted blocked modules from the process-global sys.modules before sys.meta_path.insert(0, import_guard) installed the blocking finder; a thread scheduled between those two operations could re-import a deleted blocked module and retain access to it, bypassing the intended sandbox in a multi-threaded process.

causal_research.bug_semantics: IndexFile.from_tree accepted one to three caller-controlled treeish values, appended them after GitPython's own --index-output=<temporary-index> argument, and passed the resulting argv to git read-tree without rejecting option-shaped treeish values or inserting --. An injected --index-output=<attacker-path> was therefore parsed as a later Git option and overrode the internal destination, clobbering any writable path with a Git index blob. IndexFile.reset inherited the same flaw by delegating its commit argument to from_tree, while IndexFile.merge_tree independently appended its caller-controlled base and rhs values to an unguarded read-tree invocation.

causal_research.bug_semantics: When a plugin lacked READ_FILES, PluginSandbox attempted to confine filesystem access by replacing only builtins.open with restricted_open. pathlib.Path.open/read_text/read_bytes/write_text/write_bytes and io.open retained independent file-opening paths, and pathlib/io were available to plugin code, so an untrusted plugin could read or modify paths outside the sandbox's allowed directories without passing _is_safe_path.
causal_research.flaw_origin: Commit 8a5ed7e62417441ed98b39481ac1a47510c1a9ef created the plugin sandbox and first implemented _restrict_file_operations as a single-name monkey patch: it assigned builtins.open = restricted_open but did not interpose io.open or pathlib.Path methods. causal_research.bug_semantics: A malicious repository can put traversal components in a .gitmodules section name. causal_research.bug_semantics: With allow_unsafe_options at its safe default, a caller can put an unsafe Git option such as --upload-pack=<attacker command> in the value of a single-character kwarg such as n. The guard examines only the kwarg name, which is n in the original implementation and -n after candidate reconstruction, but transform_kwarg emits the value as a separate argv token. The defect first affected fetch, pull, and push, was later copied to clone/clone_from, and was later centralized and extended to ls_remote, revision traversal/iter_commits, blame, and archive.

causal_research.bug_semantics: CredentialsPermissionChecker authorizes only credential IDs whose credential-type keys appear in a set inferred statically from unresolved node parameters. An authenticated member with edit access to a shared workflow can place another user's known credential ID on an HTTP Request node and make genericAuthType or nodeCredentialType an expression. The pre-execution checker sees the expression text rather than its runtime-resolved credential type, omits the credential ID from the ownership query, and execution later resolves and loads the unauthorized credential, allowing use or exfiltration.

causal_research.bug_semantics: With channels.msteams.groupPolicy set to allowlist, a configured teams/team/channel route allowlist was incorrectly treated as sufficient authorization when the effective sender groupAllowFrom list was empty. A message from any sender in a matched route therefore passed the route gate and skipped the sender gate, allowing an unauthorized Teams group sender to trigger bot processing and replies.

That conflated route authorization with sender authorization and first created the bypass. Commit 27dad962fee567e50ed7e293a4d8eb67cc7da8e6 later preserved the same behavior while refactoring it into an explicit ["*"] sender list; it was not the behavioral introducer.

causal_research.bug_semantics: A user who can configure a Budibase automation can supply an arbitrary HTTP(S) URL to the outgoing-webhook (and later Zapier, n8n, Slack, Discord, and Make.com) step. The server dereferenced that URL with axios/node-fetch without destination validation, so it could reach loopback, RFC1918, link-local/cloud-metadata, and other internal services (CWE-918). The REST datasource's separate guard was also fail-open by default because an unset BLACKLIST_IPS produced an empty list and isBlacklisted returned false; it neither protected automation fetches nor supplied secure defaults.
causal_research.flaw_origin: Commit 3ae82b95a31bcb6b3803d3ad8d8c5accb7606ef3 first created and registered the executable OUTGOING_WEBHOOK automation. Its run function accepted inputs.url, normalized it only by adding http://, and called axios(request) with no allowlist/denylist or resolved-address check. Commit 3d77163773d0ab37342e9e2be5d6b8797758e4eb later changed axios to node-fetch, and a3bb2e0d770fe0c66f0382aebef86faa2bbcc696 renamed/migrated the same step to TypeScript; those are implementation changes preserving the pre-existing SSRF, not introducers. Commit 564c724be11895fa6bc1766aef3a149fae3223e3 later added an opt-in REST-only blacklist whose empty-default behavior left that separate path unprotected when BLACKLIST_IPS was unset.

causal_research.bug_semantics: A post-authenticated user with Create and Modify permission can write attacker-controlled bytes outside the user's scope when an in-scope symlink points to a not-yet-existing out-of-scope file. EvalSymlinks on the link returns fs.ErrNotExist; the guard then walks the lexical path up to the link's in-scope containing directory and approves that ancestor. The subsequent OpenFile call uses O_CREATE|O_TRUNC, so the OS follows the dangling symlink and creates the target outside the scope.
causal_research.flaw_origin: Commit 847d08bdd135e5c3659f2e6dea2f0cd36617af9b introduced files.WithinScope and put it on the HTTP write path as an incomplete fix for an earlier symlink escape. Its new ErrNotExist fallback validated the nearest lexical existing ancestor and its own comment explicitly accepted dangling symlinks as best-effort. Commit 7c2c0a11b31b2bb214d741005a0b02b1764208b3 later moved the same flawed fallback into ScopedFs.within and centralized OpenFile behind that guard; the refactor preserved rather than originated the flaw.
causal_research.ai_marker: BIC commit object contains the exact trailer `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>`. Its author and committer are both Henrique Dias <mail@hacdias.com>; no bot identity is used. The commit-object co-author trailer is the attribution signal used for this verdict.
evidence: The first-party GitHub advisory https://github.com/filebrowser/filebrowser/security/advisories/GHSA-8wc8-hf36-mjh9 identifies files/scoped.go, the dangling-symlink ErrNotExist walk-up, the POST /api/resources/<link>?override=true path, affected versions <= 2.63.15, first patched version 2.63.16, and fix commit 64511ce45e3be379e965f7f4fb0929a068d5bb81.

The added comment says a dangling symlink is allowed and creation callers should treat the check as best-effort.

`git log -L ':WithinScope:files/file.go' 3406d3d7f98dfc3c16e4ff7ff4a87e3bdfe221dd` traces the function's creation to 847d08bdd135e5c3659f2e6dea2f0cd36617af9b. `git log -S'dangling symlink whose target does not yet exist' -- files/file.go files/scoped.go` returns the BIC, the later move 7c2c0a11b31b2bb214d741005a0b02b1764208b3, and the fix 64511ce45e3be379e965f7f4fb0929a068d5bb81.

Direct parent-tree verification: `git rev-list --parents -n 1 847d08bdd135e5c3659f2e6dea2f0cd36617af9b` gives sole parent 0231b7ebdfbe77a6c54027d30c4856c3fd81ee4d, and `git grep -n -e WithinScope -e EvalSymlinks 0231b7ebdfbe77a6c54027d30c4856c3fd81ee4d -- '*.go'` returns no matches. The BIC diff is therefore the first parent-to-child appearance of the flawed guard.

`git show 7c2c0a11b31b2bb214d741005a0b02b1764208b3 -- files/file.go files/scoped.go http/resource.go users/users.go` shows a refactor deleting WithinScope and creating ScopedFs.within with the same ErrNotExist lexical-parent loop and dangling-symlink best-effort comment; ScopedFs.OpenFile guards and then delegates to BasePathFs.OpenFile.

At vulnerable release commit be23ab3a15bf957928ecfed88de5ab67850c1b9c (tag v2.63.15), http/resource.go resourcePostHandler requires Create, treats the dangling link as an existing entry and requires override=true plus Modify, then writeFile calls `afs.OpenFile(dst, os.O_RDWR|os.O_CREATE|os.O_TRUNC, ...)`. files/scoped.go OpenFile first calls the flawed guard and then delegates to s.base.OpenFile, which follows the link.

The BIC added a guard intended to make symlink-backed reads and writes safe, but for a nonexistent target it discarded the unresolved leaf and approved the nearest existing lexical ancestor. A dangling final symlink is exactly the case where this inference is false: its parent is in scope while the eventual O_CREATE destination is outside. The write call was guarded by this new function in the same BIC, establishing causal content linkage. The immediate parent contains neither WithinScope nor any EvalSymlinks-based equivalent, while line-history and string-history identify 847d08bdd135e5c3659f2e6dea2f0cd36617af9b as the first writer. The later 7c2c0a11b31b2bb214d741005a0b02b1764208b3 commit is excluded as a BIC because it is a refactor that moves the unchanged faulty mechanism into ScopedFs. The advisory fix 64511ce45e3be379e965f7f4fb0929a068d5bb81 directly resolves dangling links before deciding scope and lands in the first patched tag v2.63.16. Because the real BIC commit object explicitly co-authors Claude Opus 4.8 and that same commit first writes the causally flawed fallback and its write-path use, the appropriate closed verdict is AI_ROOT_CAUSE.

causal_research.bug_semantics: TemplateContext.Reset() made a context appear safe to reuse but left its CachedTemplates dictionary intact. After one render cached a request-dependent include, a later render on the reset context found the same path in CachedTemplates and returned the old compiled Template without invoking ITemplateLoader.Load(), so content authorized for an earlier request, user, or tenant could cross the reuse boundary.
causal_research.flaw_origin: Commit 2e95889099c3ee5e7a4c0147b7355ecd309200af introduced the public Reset() API and explicitly promised safe same-thread reuse, but reset only output, global, culture, and source-file stacks. Scriban's include cache and loader-on-cache-miss path already existed in the immediate parent; omitting CachedTemplates from the newly defined reset boundary is therefore the smallest change that created the advisory's vulnerable lifecycle.

evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/scriban/scriban/security/advisories/GHSA-x6m9-38vm-2xhf identifies src/Scriban/TemplateContext.cs Reset/CachedTemplates and the include loader path, demonstrates first=admin-only then second=admin-only after Reset(), lists affected versions <= 6.6.0, and lists 7.0.0 as patched.

Thus retained state directly suppresses the request-dependent authorization/loading decision on subsequent renders.

causal_research.bug_semantics: TemplateContext caches an IObjectAccessor solely under the target's System.Type. For ordinary .NET objects, the cached TypedObjectAccessor eagerly computes its member dictionary using the context's then-current MemberFilter (and MemberRenamer). If the same TemplateContext is later reused after MemberFilter is tightened, GetMemberAccessor returns the permissive accessor already cached for that Type, so reads or writes of members now denied by policy remain available.
causal_research.flaw_origin: ace7a0ebafa6d01500f83c35975cde38d559fa3d first added TemplateContext.MemberFilter and, in the same commit, passed that mutable per-context policy into TypedObjectAccessor while leaving the pre-existing Type-only _memberAccessors cache unchanged and without invalidation. The later 2e95889099c3ee5e7a4c0147b7355ecd309200af added TemplateContext.Reset with an explicit safe-reuse contract but likewise retained the accessor cache, making the stale-policy flaw directly reachable during pooled/cross-request reuse; that later commit amplified but did not originate the flawed filter/cache composition.

Cache-line `git log -L 858,864:src/Scriban/TemplateContext.cs 8180fb6c^` shows the Type-only cache predates that commit, so the large 2017 namespace move is not misclassified as the BIC. Because lookup consults only the Type key, later member-expression access receives the old accessor and bypasses the new sandbox policy. causal_research.bug_semantics: TemplateContext.LimitToString bounded one ObjectToString conversion rather than cumulative rendered output. Each rendered expression entered a fresh top-level ObjectToString call, which reset _currentToStringLength, and StringBuilderOutput appended every resulting chunk without a render-wide cap. A template could therefore emit a near-1 MiB string in each of 1,000 loop iterations, pass the per-call check each time, and accumulate roughly 1 GiB until the host exhausted memory.
causal_research.flaw_origin: Commit b858377886c35bfedb2768de9b057377909c2e95 is the smallest real BIC: it directly added LimitToString, _currentToStringLength, and the top-level reset that made the safety counter restart for every ObjectToString conversion. Its two-file focused patch is neither a merge, aggregate, import, nor move, and its immediate parent lacks both LimitToString and _currentToStringLength. The older unconditional StringBuilderOutput append was a necessary sink but did not create the advisory-specific limit-bypass invariant; b5ac4bf30459fdc76964e3f751e16f7e96079ea7 later enabled the already-flawed limit by default. Commit 98563216488161a9edeba6c37c7cf82c98319c9b directly fixed the flaw by adding cumulative output accounting across write chunks.

causal_research.bug_semantics: POST /api/provider-nodes/validate accepts a caller-controlled baseUrl and apiKey, constructs provider URLs from baseUrl, performs server-side fetches, and forwards apiKey in Authorization headers. The later assertPublicUrl mitigation remains bypassable because it compares hostname strings without resolving DNS or revalidating redirect destinations, and its IPv4-mapped IPv6 regex expects a dotted quad even though WHATWG URL parsing canonicalizes mapped literals to hextets first. Mapped loopback/link-local literals, DNS names resolving internally, and redirects can therefore reach internal services. The custom-embedding branch also returns up to 200 bytes of most non-2xx response bodies, while other validation branches expose status/timing signals. A dashboard session is required by default, but not when requireLogin is disabled.

causal_research.bug_semantics: A page served from an attacker-controlled DNS name can retain its browser origin while DNS rebinding moves the connection to a victim's loopback Paperclip server. Paperclip's missing Host-header gate in default private local_trusted mode allowed that request to receive the implicit instance-admin board actor, create/configure a process-adapter agent with attacker-controlled command and arguments, and invoke its heartbeat/wakeup path, which passed the stored configuration to child_process.spawn as the Paperclip OS user.

causal_research.bug_semantics: The runner registration-token API exposed token creation through GET routes. The token-scope middleware derives Read versus Write from the HTTP method and classifies GET as Read, but shared.GetRegistrationToken creates a runner token when no active token exists and returns it. A leaked read-scoped user, organization, repository, or admin token could therefore obtain a runner registration credential and register a malicious Actions runner able to receive workflow jobs with access to repository source and secrets.

Its immediate parent already classified GET as Read and contained neither the route nor the helper. The later member bba250f3e99bef12bbd9a1d9d790ab8155c999d5 extended the same mechanism to user and repository routes rather than originating it.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An authenticated non-site-admin with the perm_template permission can GET the event-template add page (or edit a template writable by that user's organisation). causal_research.bug_semantics: File Browser authorized only the requested source root and, for copy or rename, the destination root, then recursively removed, renamed, or copied the whole source tree without checking rules on every descendant. An authenticated restricted user could therefore operate on an allowed parent containing a denied child, exposing or relocating the child at an allowed destination or deleting it with the parent.
causal_research.flaw_origin: Commit f6816c9a39702484ad7c5c3672209bbc4ce5f948 is the smallest reachable first-writer of the vulnerable resource operation: it created api.go, made serveAPI call c.us.Allowed only on r.URL.Path, routed DELETE to deleteHandler, and had deleteHandler recursively call c.us.fileSystem.RemoveAll on that root. Its immediate parent had no resource delete handler or equivalent user-filesystem recursive deletion. Commit 15f997faf0ff629d8da490c52c023e68a2eb7154 later added rename under the same root-only model, commit 05896697fa2730e59b8bcf6f1253da0f6fb8b5a9 later added copy while retaining only a root rule gate, and b4067cc423b1a0a9d24441bd52e2a53207a49fe9 merely split the already-vulnerable api.go handlers into resource.go rather than originating the flaw.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Access-rule authorization compared raw virtual paths as case-sensitive, slash-separated strings, while the host filesystem resolved equivalent names using its own case and separator semantics. On case-insensitive filesystems, a case variant of a denied path therefore missed the rule but reached the same file; on Windows, backslashes and traversal components likewise missed slash-based rules but were normalized by the filesystem. An authenticated user could consequently read or, subject to ordinary permissions, mutate an administrator-denied file while remaining inside the user's filesystem scope.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An authenticated BASIC app user can POST /api/attachments/:datasourceId/url because the route uses TABLE/WRITE authorization, which BASIC holds by default. getSignedUploadURL then loads the named S3 datasource's stored IAM credentials and signs PutObject for the request body's bucket and key. Normal S3 datasource configuration does not define a datasource-level bucket, so a BASIC user can obtain a presigned upload URL for any bucket writable by those credentials.

Its direct parent d180697c7d5ed9c744e2508694b29c3a94c771eb retains BUILDER. Follow-up 9d198b1b00acf8c4ef702f2ebe7758cf0485eead adds the BASIC-user HTTP-200 test, and 3e881e13186eb9da19c37deb2f55b3ab46e560b8 changes READ to WRITE without removing BASIC access; neither is the first vulnerable change.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An authenticated user with Create permission could create a TUS upload with a small finite Upload-Length, then send a PATCH body larger than Upload-Length minus Upload-Offset. tusPatchHandler streamed the entire body to the file with io.Copy before comparing the resulting offset with the cached declared length; reaching or exceeding that length merely completed the upload. The excess bytes therefore remained on disk, and repeated oversized PATCH uploads could exhaust the filesystem.
causal_research.flaw_origin: PR #5270 member 6337c4452529dfc018885a7d05cc4f1e217316c5 first made FileBrowser accept and retain the client's finite Upload-Length: it added registerUpload/getActiveUploadLength, retrieved that value in tusPatchHandler, and used it only after the pre-existing unbounded io.Copy to unregister a completed upload. Its direct parent advertised Upload-Length: -1 and neither parsed nor tracked a declared length, so the advisory-specific promise-and-bypass mechanism did not yet exist. GitHub later squash-merged the PR as 0f27c91eca581482ce4f82f6429f5dac12f8b64e.

In tag v2.63.18, http/tus_handlers.go registers Upload-Length during POST, retrieves it during PATCH, performs bytesWritten, err := io.Copy(openFile, r.Body), and only afterwards computes newOffset and completes when newOffset >= uploadLength. git log -S over http/tus_handlers.go leads to squash 0f27c91eca581482ce4f82f6429f5dac12f8b64e. Direct-parent tree https://raw.githubusercontent.com/filebrowser/filebrowser/47b3e218ad7ffac4bc62294ec589a33ef3d4ea04/http/tus_handlers.go has no activeUploads, registerUpload, getActiveUploadLength, or getUploadLength; POST ignores Upload-Length and HEAD returns Upload-Length: -1, directly proving the finite-length bypass absent. Its security-relevant invariant began when FileBrowser accepted a finite TUS Upload-Length and represented that length as the accepted upload bound. The smallest causal commit is therefore decomposed member 6337c4452529dfc018885a7d05cc4f1e217316c5, not the 2023 commit that originally added an unbounded PATCH copier, not later ttlcache/refactor members, and not aggregate squash 0f27c91eca581482ce4f82f6429f5dac12f8b64e. causal_research.bug_semantics: An authenticated user whose same-scope account has Perm.Download=false can call GET /api/resources/<path>?checksum=<md5|sha1|sha256|sha512>. resourceGetHandler invokes FileInfo.Checksum, which opens and reads the file, then serializes the digest, without first enforcing Perm.Download. The response is therefore a same-scope content-hash oracle that can confirm guessed content, reveal changes, and support offline brute force of low-entropy files; it does not bypass path/scope authorization.
causal_research.flaw_origin: The first reachable v2 implementation commit, 42227d9edd7ce613e8b6c0ad62c8cad16cf77266, added both the granular Download permission in types/user.go and the new http/resource.go checksum branch, but the branch checked no Download permission. The old immediate-parent model had no Download permission, so this member commit first created the relevant permission-bypass mechanism. Master later squashed PR #575 into 12b2c215221696de58431093e01eeff7a5414471. The 2026 commit 1e03feadb550e4414b5589a6a8df57f538efba15 fixed content-returning paths for CVE-2026-35606 but merely left the older checksum flaw in place; it did not write the vulnerable checksum lines.

PR #575 member 42227d9edd7ce613e8b6c0ad62c8cad16cf77266 is the smallest reconstructable commit that simultaneously introduced the Download permission and rewrote the checksum operation without enforcing it. The member's direct diff and parent tree establish immediate-parent absence. The later master squash 12b2c215221696de58431093e01eeff7a5414471 merely aggregated that member and is excluded as the BIC. The vulnerable combination is demonstrably present in v2.0.0, survives the incomplete 1e03feadb550e4414b5589a6a8df57f538efba15 remediation, and is removed by 6c69b5cd895e15b29e563200a9a6dfc27b06525e at the v2.63.19 boundary. causal_research.bug_semantics: On a fresh instance with no password configured, check_auth() deliberately admitted every request. POST /api/settings nevertheless accepted the ownership-establishing _set_password pseudo-setting: save_settings() hashed the attacker-chosen value into settings.json as password_hash, turning authentication on. A remote unauthenticated first caller could therefore choose the initial credential, authenticate (and, after the later session-continuity change, receive a session immediately), and lock out the intended operator. The missing invariant was that the unauthenticated disabled-auth state must not permit a non-local client to perform the transition that establishes the first trust root.
causal_research.flaw_origin: The optional-password feature commit introduced both halves of the flaw together: api/auth.py made check_auth() return true whenever no password existed, while api/config.py made the already-generic /api/settings save path interpret untrusted _set_password as authority to persist the first password. It added no locality, bootstrap token, or existing-owner check around that transition. A later commit only added automatic cookie issuance; it did not originate the takeover because an attacker could already log in with the password they selected.

causal_research.bug_semantics: A logged-in user could submit a saved graph configuration whose config_json was checked only for syntactically valid JSON. The server stored and returned the object without a property allowlist; an administrator's list included every user's saved configurations. Loading one parsed the stored JSON and applyConfig spread every property of attacker-controlled stixStyles or mispStyles entries into GRAPH_CONFIG. Those style maps were then passed to Pivotick as nodeStyleMap/defaultNodeStyle, and Pivotick interpreted a supplied svgIcon as HTML, so viewing/loading the saved configuration could execute attacker script in another user's browser.
causal_research.flaw_origin: Commit a0a9834b21b40ab570db54e1c6e6c2cf100b5f9a introduced the complete unsafe saved-configuration path in one focused feature commit: the graph_config model and save/list routes, unrestricted JSON persistence, the saved-config loader, and applyConfig's unrestricted style-object spreads. Its immediate parent had none of the graph-config persistence, loading, or patch-application mechanism, making this ordinary one-parent feature commit the smallest reconstructable BIC rather than the later branch merge or a release commit.

causal_research.bug_semantics: The conversion-history details endpoint reads a ConversionHistory row by caller-supplied history_id and serializes retained input_text, old_output_text, and new_output_text. Once ordinary conversion deletion became a soft delete, the parent conversion and its history remained in the database. The later normal parent lookup hid inactive conversions and returned None, while the authorization guard denied only when the parent was truthy and invisible; a deleted parent therefore skipped denial and its history payload was returned. The endpoint was anonymous immediately after the soft-delete change and remained exploitable by authenticated requesters after the later login hardening.
causal_research.flaw_origin: Commit bf868699adf960e7f812d30ccc3f1fa28131ba34 is the smallest causal BIC. Its direct parent hard-deleted the conversion and deleted its histories through the ORM delete-orphan relationship and database ON DELETE CASCADE. Commit 37d7ba64638ad78f4604725f81bafac497ca235a was later partial hardening: it added login and visibility checks, but preserved the already-live deleted-parent disclosure with a truthiness-guarded check; it did not originate the vulnerability.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Remote-data DOM XSS in the MISP event browser: the server accepts an operator-selected remote MISP instance, copies that instance's event fields into JSON, and the browser interpolates those values into template strings assigned to innerHTML. A malicious or compromised remote MISP can therefore inject markup or script-capable content through event IDs, information, organization/date/count/threat fields, tag names and colors, TLP/distribution labels, or flash/error text; unvalidated tag colors also enter inline CSS.
causal_research.flaw_origin: Commit b9f40af30de83fa44a14a3b0263df26192696b48 added the remote-MISP connection/browser feature and, in the same atomic commit, passed remote response fields through website/web/convert/convert.py and rendered them with div.innerHTML, overlay.innerHTML, and tr.innerHTML in website/web/templates/convert/misp_to_stix.html. The core mistake was treating remote-derived strings and colors as trusted HTML/CSS instead of creating DOM nodes and assigning textContent plus validating colors. Commit 26ecb7e6a608b5be73fa552928e00bef7cac4f22 later expanded selection/distribution behavior and added further instances of the same mechanism, but b9f40af30de83fa44a14a3b0263df26192696b48 is the earliest and smallest real BIC for the vulnerable event-browser mechanism.

causal_research.bug_semantics: rConfig deliberately disabled Laravel self-registration with Auth::routes(['register' => false]), but a later bare Auth::routes() call registered the framework's default registration endpoints again. An unauthenticated POST /register therefore reached RegisterController, whose create() method omitted role; the users.role database column defaulted to Admin, and the RegistersUsers flow authenticated the newly created account. The attacker consequently obtained a logged-in Administrator account without invitation, approval, or prior credentials.
causal_research.flaw_origin: The smallest first-writer is 5ae01b3781de867baad1a8aa8aebfc3448812f68. In the multiple-SSO feature commit, routes/web.php gained the single causally decisive line Auth::routes(); between the new SAML logout and provider redirect routes. causal_research.bug_semantics: LocalFolderExtractor forms a filesystem path from an attacker-controlled RAR entry name and, before the direct fix, accepts it when its canonical-path string starts with the destination canonical-path string. This is not a path-component containment test: for destination /tmp/extract, ../extract_evil/pwned.txt canonicalizes under the sibling /tmp/extract_evil yet still has the lexical prefix /tmp/extract, allowing FileOutputStream to write attacker-controlled archive content outside the extraction directory. The same boundary defect affects directory entries.
causal_research.flaw_origin: The exact sibling-path write was already possible before the public Git history. Later commits 75cb6a58c9b3ca08db954eec241b91a5331dd632 and 3b645d991563dd8933f6efab135cd76a43a92d6b copied/moved the extraction implementation. Commit e60b915f8932c08b9b6874a97f00676decba069a added a defective canonical-string prefix guard, but its direct parent remained exploitable by the advisory's same ../extract_evil path, so e60b915 is an incomplete mitigation rather than the vulnerability introducer.

causal_research.bug_semantics: awxkit's custom PyYAML Loader registers !include and !import and sends attacker-controlled scalar, sequence, or mapping values to extractFile(). Before the fix, extractFile() joined those values to the importing stream's directory, expanded them with glob.glob(), converted matches to absolute paths, and opened and recursively parsed them without rejecting absolute paths, '..' traversal, or symlink escapes. A victim who runs 'awx --conf.format yaml import' on crafted YAML can therefore disclose arbitrary locally readable YAML-formatted files; this is a client-side confidentiality flaw requiring user interaction.
causal_research.flaw_origin: The vulnerable Loader/extractFile code first appears in ansible/awx public history in 9616cc6f7856523ebf6d1580443313296c9f6507, but that commit is explicitly titled 'import awxkit' and adds 101 files with 10,479 lines. Its direct parent lacks awxkit/awxkit/yaml_file.py, and the associated two-commit range contains only that import plus an awxkit CI follow-up. It is therefore an aggregate public-history gateway for pre-existing awxkit/towerkit code, not the smallest commit that authored the flaw. The pre-import authoring history is unavailable, so the protocol-valid BIC cannot be named.

causal_research.bug_semantics: The advisory combines two x-proxy-path trust failures. In admin.ts, an attacker-controlled request header was inserted verbatim into served HTML, JavaScript, and CSS; because those header-dependent responses also lacked Vary and private/no-store cache controls, the reflection enabled direct or shared-cache-poisoning XSS on the admin origin. Separately, specialpages.ts passed a sanitizer that allowed leading slashes and then concatenated its result into a 302 Location. An x-proxy-path value of //evil.example therefore produced //evil.example/p/<encoded-pad>, which a browser follows as a protocol-relative cross-origin redirect.
causal_research.flaw_origin: There are two independently introduced mechanisms. The admin reflection first appeared in human-authored commit 3e9c90e994d4af71ac8f49668f48caf61ef1b55d, not in the advisory's cited 63e9b2d4eb303cd341022591bdf9484584db36e3. The open-redirect mechanism first appeared when retained PR #7710 member f784c8c47c16e184b3ef3bdbf84485d4e5c42eb2 changed a safe relative redirect into an absolute redirect prefixed by sanitizeProxyPath(req), whose character filter preserved a leading //. That member was represented on the public branch by squash 451bd9c3ebb0dded99dd0ff21811ee00e0940c29. The selected introducer is the smallest BIC for the advisory's AI-authored open-redirect component; the separate older admin-XSS origin is retained for complete lifecycle attribution.

causal_research.bug_semantics: The unauthenticated GET /tokenTransfer/:uuid handler retrieved a token-bearing transfer record but never checked its createdAt timestamp, never removed the record after redemption, and serialized the whole record in the response after setting the author cookie. Anyone who learned a random transfer UUID through an out-of-band leak could therefore redeem it indefinitely and repeatedly, read the raw author token despite the later HttpOnly-cookie design, and persistently impersonate the originating author.
causal_research.flaw_origin: PR #7228 was squash-landed as 41cb6803d2ac71cadf42f4aa88f37c85275a3879, but its six public member commits are reconstructable. Member 35519176db4bf6ed0e09d24cc1de58f85552cc24 is the smallest BIC: it first added the persistent db.set keyed by a UUID, wrote createdAt without any redemption-time check, added the unauthenticated GET lookup without deletion, and returned the stored token record with res.send(token). Its immediate parent 409b43f7f4aa9ba4107fc2b329d55f8a05bfcebe contained only a seven-line POST stub and none of those vulnerable operations. causal_research.bug_semantics: On Linux/Unix, LocalFolderExtractor first constructs and canonicalizes new File(destination, archiveEntryName) while backslashes in the untrusted RAR name are still literal filename characters. A name such as '..\..\tmp\evil' therefore passes the destination-prefix check. If the file does not exist, makeFile then splits that same name on backslashes and rejoins the components with File.separator, turning the previously literal '..' components into real '/' traversal. extract subsequently opens FileOutputStream on that reconstructed path and writes attacker-controlled archive content outside the extraction directory.
causal_research.flaw_origin: The causal flaw is the two-stage, inconsistent interpretation of an archive pathname: validation and use do not operate on the same normalized representation. The backslash-splitting/reconstruction and write path first appear in the repository's root initial-import commit 6f32323c983015d96c64084418793853f514b519 in testutil/src/main/java/de/innosystec/unrar/testutil/ExtractArchive.java. That implementation was later promoted and moved through production paths without changing the mechanism; e60b915f8932c08b9b6874a97f00676decba069a added canonical-path validation but left it before the separator reinterpretation, creating the advisory's explicit validation bypass rather than originating the underlying arbitrary-write mechanism.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Etherpad generated import/export working-file names in the shared process temporary directory from Math.random(), then used ordinary write, rename, and converter operations that follow existing symbolic links. A local low-privilege user who can predict a token and pre-create the corresponding /tmp path as a symlink can redirect Etherpad's file operation to a target writable by the Etherpad process, causing disclosure or overwrite; import output can contain attacker-influenced converted document content.

Commits 4fc4a3538148bc995fff989794e91779ed4c847f and b0976a292f70c2c6d344bafd2793aed09027f74b later changed the token formula to Math.random()*0xFFFFFFFF, reducing it to the advisory's exact 32-bit form, but they did not originate the insecure shared-temp predictable-name mechanism.

causal_research.bug_semantics: The Admin Console gadget endpoint passes the request-controlled #{param.gadget} value to gf.getGadgetModule, which accepts a path or complete URL and parses the referenced XML. JSFTemplating then resolves handler input in a context where a resulting #{...} string is evaluated again, while gadget.jsf emits pageSession.gadget.text with escaping disabled. Attacker-controlled gadget XML can therefore inject server-side EL; the unrestricted resolver exposed class/getClass, constructors, static methods, and static fields, making the injection capable of remote code execution.

causal_research.bug_semantics: The privileged /admin/gateways/test flow performed a security decision on DNS answers obtained while validating the submitted hostname, then gave an httpx-based ResilientHttpClient a URL containing that same hostname. The client therefore performed an independent connection-time resolution. An attacker controlling DNS could return a public address for validation and then rebind the hostname to a private, loopback, link-local, or cloud-metadata address for the actual request, bypassing the SSRF network checks.

SecurityValidator._validate_ssrf used socket.getaddrinfo for the check, but the member did not preserve or bind the checked address for the later connection. The repository landed PR #3115 as squash d549137791f10c59c00ec3e89cb55cd560a8248f; later allowlist work made the limitation more explicit but did not originate it.

causal_research.bug_semantics: The unauthenticated static-download route passes request.getParameter("version") into BaseUtils.replaceFileNameAndExtension without validating it. For a request to the route base (/file/static/noauth in the renamed endpoint, formerly /downloadFile/static/noauth), the path-derived fileName is "noauth", whose full-path component is empty, so the helper replaces it entirely with attacker-controlled version. A value such as ../../etc/passwd is then handed to FileUtils.readFile(APP_DOWNLOAD_FOLDER_PATH, fileName, ...), which constructs new File(APP_DOWNLOAD_FOLDER_PATH, fileName) and can escape the intended download directory, exposing arbitrary readable files without authentication.

The already-existing security rule exempted /downloadFile/static/noauth/** from authentication, making this new trust-boundary error remotely reachable immediately.

causal_research.bug_semantics: deepExtend() enumerated attacker-controlled own keys and used Reflect.has() on the merge receiver. For a JSON-parsed __proto__ key, Reflect.has({}, '__proto__') is true through Object.prototype's inherited accessor; because both resolved values are objects, the recursive branch calls extendObject(Object.prototype, attackerValue), and the attacker's nested keys are then assigned onto Object.prototype. Every subsequently created ordinary object inherits the injected properties, enabling application-dependent integrity, availability, or authorization failures wherever untrusted data reaches deepExtend().
causal_research.flaw_origin: Commit ece027428a9a5755916f159a5760665be9cc89a6 changed the receiver test from !o1.hasOwnProperty(key) to !Reflect.has(o1, key) while retaining recursive merging and no forbidden-key filter. That semantic change made inherited __proto__ look like an existing object-valued destination and redirected recursion into Object.prototype. Earlier code could alter the returned object's own prototype via __proto__ assignment, but the advisory's realm-wide Object.prototype write primitive was absent until this commit.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An initialized XKB client can first grow xkb->map->num_types to 255 with a SetMap request carrying XkbSetMapResizeTypes, then send firstType=255 and nTypes=10. CheckKeyTypes() accepts firstType because it rejects only firstType > num_types, computes the client-controlled sum nMaps=265 without bounding it to the caller's 256-entry mapWidths stack array, and writes mapWidthRtrn[i + firstType] for the supplied types. The writes to indices 256 through 264 overflow nine bytes into adjacent stack state, allowing a server crash and potentially privilege escalation when the X server is privileged.

Its imported xkb/xkb.c begins with an Xorg CVS revision dated 2000 and a 1993 copyright, so the vulnerable source predates the 2003 Git import. The retained repository does not contain the external CVS/X Consortium commit that first combined the fixed 256-entry stack array, unchecked firstType+nTypes sum, and indexed write.

causal_research.bug_semantics: On a glamor-backed X server, glamor_font_get() sized a CPU-side font-atlas heap buffer and each glyph slot from the font's declared maxbounds, but copied each bitmap using that glyph's unchecked GLYPHWIDTHBYTES and GLYPHHEIGHTPIXELS metrics. libXfont2's PCF parser did not recompute maxbounds from the per-glyph records, so an authenticated X client could supply a PCF whose individual metrics exceeded (or were negative relative to) maxbounds; drawing text then made the row memcpy write attacker-controlled bytes beyond the allocated atlas, with negative values also permitting unsigned/size_t wrap.

That new mismatch is the exact heap-buffer-overflow mechanism.

causal_research.bug_semantics: When the optional webhook server is enabled, it listens on all interfaces and accepts POST requests containing an attacker-controlled exec string. Authentication is fail-open: WebhookServer.authenticate returns true whenever the configured token is empty, a state the configuration comments explicitly describe as 'empty = no auth'. The handler then dispatches req.Exec to a shell with -c/-Command. Thus an attacker who supplies a nonempty, reconstructable session_key (and a project when multiple projects are configured) can execute an arbitrary shell program as the cc-connect process without a credential. The shell interpretation of exec is an intentional feature; the security failure is exposing that full shell capability across a network endpoint while treating an omitted token as authorization.

causal_research.bug_semantics: For a window drawable, do_get_buffers allocated only count + 1 DRI2BufferPtr slots, filled count client-requested slots, and then used arithmetic attachment counters to decide whether to append implicit front buffers. With at least two DRI2BufferBackLeft requests and one DRI2BufferFrontLeft request, need_real_front remained positive even though FrontLeft was already present, so a redundant real-front pointer was appended at buffers[count]. The FrontLeft request also made need_fake_front positive, so the fake-front pointer was then written at buffers[count + 1], one pointer beyond the heap allocation. The DRI2GetBuffers and DRI2GetBuffersWithFormat request paths both called this helper, allowing a local X client to crash the server or potentially escalate privileges when it ran as root.
causal_research.flaw_origin: Commit ff6c7764c2909e4126403b7211faa6c58556b341 replaced the parent's bulk CreateBuffers path with per-attachment allocation and introduced need_real_front++/-- alongside the existing fake-front accounting, while retaining an allocation sized for only one implicit attachment. The parent could append at most one fake front and therefore respected its count + 1 capacity; the new combination could append both a redundant real front and a fake front. Treating attachment presence as signed counts rather than boolean presence broke the allocation invariant.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An X client can send XkbSetMap with a non-canonical key type whose one-byte numLevels is as large as 255. CheckKeyTypes accepted every positive value and stored it even though downstream code assumes at most XkbMaxShiftLevel (63). A later core ChangeKeyboardMapping reaches XkbUpdateKeyTypesFromCore and XkbKeyTypesForCoreSymbols, where the tainted level count becomes groupsWidth and XKB_OFFSET(g,l) indexes a 252-entry XkbMaxSymsPerKey stack buffer; at width 255 the maximum index is 1019. The same oversized key geometry can also make XkbChangeTypesOfKey copy excessive symbols and actions into its fixed oldSyms and oldActs stack arrays, yielding three client-triggerable stack overflows and possible crash or privilege escalation when the server is privileged.
causal_research.flaw_origin: The causal mechanism is the combination of CheckKeyTypes validating only numLevels >= 1 and the XKB conversion/resizing paths using fixed XkbMaxShiftLevel * XkbNumKbdGroups stack arrays without independently bounding stored non-canonical type widths. All of those lines already appear in the repository's 2003 R6.6 vendor baseline import, whose immediate parent contains no xkb tree. That 609-file baseline aggregate imported pre-existing X11/XFree86 code rather than authoring the mechanism, so the smallest original change and its parent are beyond this Git history. The 2025 CVE-2025-26597 fix changed only the nGroups == 0 action-resize path and did not introduce this excessive-numLevels path.

causal_research.bug_semantics: With federation enabled, NodeBB authenticated the HTTP-signature key against the ActivityPub activity actor and required object.id to have that actor's origin, but did not bind object.attributedTo to the authenticated actor. A remote actor could therefore send a signed Create whose object.id was on the attacker's origin but whose attributedTo was a bare local numeric uid such as 1. The inbound mock copied attributedTo into the post/message uid; actors.assert filtered numeric identifiers out and its false result was ignored, after which topic or chat persistence treated the attacker-chosen local uid as the author.
causal_research.flaw_origin: Commit f74775365a57262488434c920c7b805608b761c7 first made the unsafe attribution mapping remotely exploitable: it added inbox.create, took only req.body.object for authorship, passed the untrusted object through activitypub.mocks.post, and persisted the resulting postData without comparing attributedTo to the authenticated req.body.actor. The unsafe mocks.post assignment had been prepared in f1e5e5a0ad4cc6d5a02bf9bc952e524fe2f58458 and moved by 06e1583461f034d68c8c3c6d69547b06ad6ab3b5, but f74775365a57262488434c920c7b805608b761c7 is the smallest commit that connected it to the inbound Create attack surface and made the remote post-forgery path real.

The commit has one parent, so it is neither a merge nor a squash aggregate.

History cross-checks show the precursor assignment `attributedTo: uid` originated in f1e5e5a0ad4cc6d5a02bf9bc952e524fe2f58458, was only moved by refactor 06e1583461f034d68c8c3c6d69547b06ad6ab3b5, and became remotely reachable in f74775365a57262488434c920c7b805608b761c7. causal_research.bug_semantics: During ListFonts/ListFontsWithInfo font-alias resolution, a client-controlled fonts.alias target accepted by libXfont2 can be 257-1023 bytes, while the server used 256-byte XLFDMAXFONTNAMELEN-backed stack-resident tmp_pattern and current.pattern buffers. The alias paths copied resolvedlen or namelen bytes into those buffers without a preceding bound check, so a client that adds a crafted directory with SetFontPath and requests the alias can overflow the stack, crash the server, or potentially escalate privileges when the server is privileged.

causal_research.bug_semantics: The unauthenticated /cgi-bin/api.values.get handler in the Grandstream GXP1600 firmware's 32-bit ARM /app/bin/gs_web binary parses the attacker-controlled request parameter as colon-delimited identifiers and copies each non-colon byte into a 64-byte stack buffer without checking the identifier length. An identifier longer than 63 bytes writes beyond that buffer, and repeated colon-delimited identifiers let an attacker place multiple terminating NUL bytes, overwrite saved registers including PC, build a ROP chain, and invoke system() as root.
causal_research.flaw_origin: The flawed bounds-free identifier-copy loop belongs to Grandstream's proprietary GXP1600 firmware, not rapid7/metasploit-framework. Its source and version-control history are not public, so the exact introducing source commit is beyond the public-history boundary. Metasploit commit 08efa9cd16f254bfc8f2f4cee0550f3a851e0aa5 merely added an exploit for the already-existing device flaw after fixed firmware 1.0.7.81 had been released; it did not write the vulnerable /app/bin/gs_web code.
causal_research.ai_marker: unavailable: there is no public BIC commit object for Grandstream's proprietary /app/bin/gs_web source, so BIC author, committer, bot identity, Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, and other trailer checks cannot be performed; no AI conclusion is drawn from the later Metasploit exploit commit
evidence: Rapid7's first-party disclosure (https://www.rapid7.com/blog/post/ve-cve-2026-2329-critical-unauthenticated-stack-buffer-overflow-in-grandstream-gxp1600-voip-phones-fixed) identifies the vulnerable component as the native 32-bit ARM /app/bin/gs_web firmware binary and decompiles its api.values.get handler: attacker-controlled request_buffer bytes are appended to small_buffer[64] while part_length is incremented without a bound check. It documents PC control and the repeated-colon/NUL technique used to construct a ROP chain and execute commands as root.

The disclosure tested vulnerable firmware 1.0.7.79 and says users must upgrade to 1.0.7.81 or above. Its timeline records that Grandstream made 1.0.7.81 available, reaffirmed the issue resolved in that release, and that Rapid7 independently verified remediation by reverse engineering the public firmware. This is binary verification, not a public source commit.

Grandstream's release notes (https://firmware.grandstream.com/Release_Note_GXP16xx_1.0.7.81.pdf) list 1.0.7.81 for all six affected models, date it 2026-01-30, and include 'Fixed some security vulnerabilities.' The preceding 1.0.7.80 is dated 2025-12-31. The Metasploit module's description at modules/exploits/linux/http/grandstream_gxp1600_unauth_rce.rb:19-23 states that every firmware version below 1.0.7.81 is affected, and its check at lines 105-117 classifies version < 1.0.7.81 as vulnerable and 1.0.7.81 or later as safe.
NVD's analyzed CVE-2026-2329 record identifies the affected products as Grandstream GXP1610/GXP1615/GXP1620/GXP1625/GXP1628/GXP1630 firmware and CWE-121, not Metasploit Framework.

causal_research.bug_semantics: A remote Bluetooth device can supply an EIR name element whose field_len is 254, making eir_parse pass data_len 253 to name2utf8. On the non-UTF-8 conversion path, name2utf8 used strncpy with that attacker-controlled length to copy into utf8_name[HCI_MAX_NAME_LENGTH + 2]. HCI_MAX_NAME_LENGTH is 248, so the 250-byte stack array is overrun by three bytes; the missing terminator can also make the subsequent stripping and duplication read beyond the array. Discovery therefore permits a radio-adjacent unauthenticated peer to crash bluetoothd and potentially corrupt control data.
causal_research.flaw_origin: Commit 155fa21473ada6d3e7773175186badd4bc0fde22 first added src/eir.c:name2utf8 and coupled the fixed 250-byte utf8_name array to strncpy(..., len), where len is derived from the untrusted EIR element length and can be 253. Although the subject calls the change a move, the removed src/event.c code copied at the fixed MGMT_MAX_NAME_LENGTH bound, while the newly added EIR helper introduced the attacker-length copy; it is therefore the smallest causal introducer rather than a pure move. Later commit 218db700f49370bc07ce1e6d609d28d846470d99 changed character conversion but retained the already-vulnerable array and copy.
causal_research.ai_marker: absent: the raw commit object for 155fa21473ada6d3e7773175186badd4bc0fde22 names Johan Hedberg <johan.hedberg@intel.com> as both author and committer and contains only the subject 'core: Move UTF-8 validation of device names into eir.c'; it has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, Assisted-by, bot identity, or other AI trailer/marker.
evidence: The first-party BlueZ advisory https://github.com/bluez/bluez/security/advisories/GHSA-68h6-5qgp-3975 identifies src/eir.c:name2utf8, affected release 5.86, and patched commit 381b5d0d208972586282116d333865ba93b8dec2. It explains that field_len 254 yields data_len 253 and a three-byte overflow of the 250-byte array.

git show --format=fuller --patch 381b5d0d208972586282116d333865ba93b8dec2 shows the direct fix adding 'len = MIN(len, HCI_MAX_NAME_LENGTH);' immediately before memset/strncpy in src/eir.c. The commit message also records the remote EIR/advertising attack path and the possible unterminated follow-on reads.

At fix parent c73fa2f9ae2d366cb8a4f101fa9a5ccd9f33a4ea, git blame -L 136,150 -- src/eir.c assigns the function, utf8_name declaration, memset, strncpy(..., len), g_strstrip, and g_strdup to 155fa21473ada6d3e7773175186badd4bc0fde22; only the character-conversion call is later (218db700f49370bc07ce1e6d609d28d846470d99).

git log --all --reverse -S 'strncpy(utf8_name, (char *) name, len)' -- src/eir.c returns 155fa21473ada6d3e7773175186badd4bc0fde22 as the first addition and 8c81ab108b09154b884b1b0549dc9c23ffe3ec6f as its later removal, confirming the smallest source-level origin.

git show 155fa21473ada6d3e7773175186badd4bc0fde22 shows the new helper and the EIR_NAME_SHORT/EIR_NAME_COMPLETE call name2utf8(data, data_len). In the same parser, a first field_len of 254 with eir_len 255 passes the bounds check and computes data_len = field_len - 1 = 253. git grep at that commit confirms HCI_MAX_NAME_LENGTH is 248 in lib/hci.h, so the destination is 250 bytes.

Immediate-parent tree verification used git grep at 0f75430e0c827ad069f616e02563237b1099518e: there is no name2utf8 and no src/eir.c attacker-length strncpy; the only matching src/event.c copy is strncpy(utf8_name, name, MGMT_MAX_NAME_LENGTH), a fixed bound into MGMT_MAX_NAME_LENGTH + 1. Version checks show the BIC is not an ancestor of tag 4.101 but is an ancestor of tag 5.0 and of the advisory's affected tag 5.86 (74770b1fd2be612f9c2cf807db81fcdcc35e6560). Tag 5.86 contains the vulnerable strncpy and no clamp. The fix is not in tag 5.86, while 5.86 is an ancestor of 381b5d0d208972586282116d333865ba93b8dec2, placing the fix after the affected boundary.

AuthenticationHeaderResolver.resolveWorkspace then trusts X-Airbyte-Workspace-Id before any resource-derived header, so the role check is performed against the attacker's workspace while the endpoint handler operates on the victim resource; no later ownership comparison reconnects the authorization decision to the resource.

The raw-body header extractor already existed in the parent, so this commit is the smallest repository commit that completed the vulnerable per-workspace authorization mechanism.

causal_research.bug_semantics: When the opt-in Management API is enabled with its token left empty, its authentication middleware treats the empty secret as successful authentication. The server listens on all interfaces at port 9820, and an unauthenticated remote POST to /api/v1/cron can copy attacker-controlled JSON exec text into a persisted CronJob. The cron scheduler identifies a nonempty Exec as a shell job and ultimately runs that text through the configured shell, so the attacker obtains command execution when the job fires; later code also added an immediate /api/v1/cron/{id}/exec trigger, but that was not necessary for the original scheduled-execution path.
causal_research.flaw_origin: The vulnerable trust-boundary crossing was created in one change: c2681402a7686294174a263e31245a52d4fea380 added the network-facing Management API, deliberately made authenticate return true for an empty token, registered the cron endpoints behind that fail-open middleware, and assigned untrusted req.Exec directly to CronJob.Exec. The shell-capable CronJob and its sh -c execution sink already existed in the parent; c2681402 is the smallest commit that made that sink reachable from an unauthenticated remote management request.

causal_research.bug_semantics: A template-controlled reverse range such as (100000000..1) makes evalRangeToken charge high - low + 1, a large negative count. Limiter.use accepted that negative count and added it to its cumulative base, creating artificial budget credit. Later append/replace operations could therefore exceed the configured memoryLimit; flattening the resulting large V8 cons-string could terminate the Node.js process, producing denial of service.
causal_research.flaw_origin: Commit 2af297f81ac465feb3277ba7b92f7236409370b0 added ctx.memoryLimit.use(high - low + 1) to src/render/expression.ts without constraining the charge to a non-negative range size. The pre-existing Limiter.use implementation accepted and accumulated signed counts, so this new attacker-controlled negative callsite completed the underflow/budget-bypass mechanism. Reverse ranges themselves return an empty array because range(start, stop) loops only while start < stop, making the negative charge pure budget credit rather than a matching allocation.

causal_research.bug_semantics: LiquidJS promised to bound each render with renderLimit, but Render.renderTemplates checked elapsed time only inside its loop over template nodes. An empty for or tablerow body parses to an empty templates array, so every attacker-controlled collection iteration calls renderTemplates([]), executes no check, and consumes CPU linearly up to the separate memoryLimit while bypassing the configured wall-clock budget.

The existing for and tablerow tags could pass an empty body array once per collection element, so placing the new security check exclusively inside the zero-trip inner loop created the bypass at the moment the guard was introduced.

causal_research.bug_semantics: The default-registered strip_html filter applied one global regular expression containing unbounded lazy script, style, comment, and generic-tag alternatives directly to attacker-controlled template data. On many opener tokens without a matching closer, V8 retries an alternative at each '<' and scans the remaining suffix looking for the absent terminator, producing quadratic work on the single Node.js event-loop thread. memoryLimit did not bound that CPU work because it charged only the input string length before String.replace ran.

That functional-parity change first introduced the unbounded lazy alternatives and therefore the vulnerable repeated-suffix search; later moves and expansions preserved or broadened the same mechanism rather than originating it.

causal_research.bug_semantics: LiquidJS accepted a lexically resolved template pathname as proof that the file opened was inside a configured root, partials, or layouts directory. Node then followed symlinks at the file operation, so a symlink placed under an allowed template directory could point to an arbitrary readable file outside that directory and include, render, or layout would parse and render the external target. The assigned advisory records liquidjs <= 10.25.2 as vulnerable and 10.25.3 as the first patched version.

The immediate parent had neither handleCache/renderFile nor tags/include.js, so the causal filesystem-template load path was absent; later loader extractions, path checks, and file moves merely preserved or re-expressed this same symlink-following flaw.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Preact distinguishes genuine VNodes by giving them an own constructor value of undefined. In the affected client renderer, the gate became `if (newVNode.constructor != UNDEFINED) return NULL`; JavaScript loose equality treats null and undefined as equal, so a JSON-parsed attacker object shaped as a VNode and carrying `constructor: null` passes the gate. If an application passes that unsanitized object into the render tree, Preact consumes its attacker-controlled type and props as a VNode and can inject HTML, with script execution possible where CSP or other defenses do not stop it. The companion loose `childVNode.constructor == UNDEFINED` check also admits null as the VNode sentinel in child processing. The server-side preact-render-to-string path was not affected.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An unauthenticated network client can complete the RTMP handshake/connect/createStream/publish sequence and receive NetStream.Publish.Start because SRS treats RTMP publishing as permitted unless an operator explicitly enables a vhost security policy (or supplies a separate hook/token control). In the default state, SrsSecurity::check returns success immediately when security.enabled is false, so the publish path has no mandatory authentication boundary.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An attacker can place OSC/CSI control bytes in a filesystem entry name. causal_research.bug_semantics: A backend user with backend.manage_branding can persist attacker-controlled custom_css. BrandSetting::compileCss() concatenates that value into LESS input, and LESS escape syntax can preserve a literal </style><script> payload in the compiled output. The shared backend layout emits BrandSetting::renderCss() inside a style element, so an unsanitized cache miss or cache hit permits stored XSS for later backend-page viewers.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An authenticated backend user holding any one granular Theme Editor permission could enter Cms\Controllers\Index because the controller authorization was an OR gate, while AJAX code trusted the request-supplied template type without consistently checking the permission mapped to that type. The user could therefore reach pages, partials, layouts, content, or assets outside the granted scope. AssetList was also registered without requiring cms.manage_assets, and its upload path omitted the active-theme validation applied to other mutating asset handlers.

Its direct parent lacks both source paths and the granular permission-bearing implementation, so the vulnerable boundary first exists in this commit. The commit directly adds the affected files rather than moving them and has one parent with no public constituent commits to decompose.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An authenticated backend user could submit the self-service account save handler with an attacker-chosen form_context such as update. FormController trusted that POST value over the server-selected myaccount context, so Users::formExtendFields treated the request as an administrative user form and admitted role, individual-permission, and superuser-related fields into the form widget's save data. The handler still selected the attacker's own User model, allowing protected authorization attributes to be mass-updated and the account to gain higher backend privileges.

causal_research.bug_semantics: ScpClient.Download(string, DirectoryInfo) starts a recursive SCP receive and trusts the filename captured from each server-controlled C (file) or D (directory) protocol record. It joins that unvalidated value to the current local download directory and then creates the directory or opens the file for writing. A malicious, compromised, or MITM server can therefore supply ../ components (and, after the later Path.Combine form, rooted paths) to escape the caller's destination and create or overwrite any path writable by the client process. Exploitation requires the victim to initiate a recursive directory download from the attacker-controlled endpoint.
causal_research.flaw_origin: Commit d96c93abb2f9409281bfb12d2da8622470a4b3e3 first added ScpClient and its recursive directory-download implementation. In Renci.SshClient/Renci.SshNet/ScpClient.NET.cs it parsed arbitrary remote C/D record names and used them directly in local directory creation and FileInfo construction without requiring a single safe path component. Commit 266dbaefe6c1f2bff2ea00c9ac14a246d37079d9 later changed the string concatenations to Path.Combine but did not introduce the trust-boundary flaw; renames, line-ending changes, and the 2023 partial-class merge likewise only carried the existing mechanism forward.

Code run there could make same-origin fetch requests with the victim's session, enumerate the victim's user/workspace credentials, receive decrypted credential data from credentials.getCredentials, and exfiltrate API keys, OAuth tokens, and passwords. The workspace form of getCredentials also authorized the supplied workspace but, at the vulnerable snapshot, did not bind the requested credential ID to that workspace.

causal_research.bug_semantics: With saveLogs enabled, a caller authorized to execute an action can supply a nonempty, nonduplicate StartAction UniqueTrackingId containing slash and .. segments. OliveTin accepts that string, stores it as the log entry's ExecutionTrackingID, interpolates it into the .yaml and .log filenames, and passes those names to path.Join. path.Join cleans the traversal segments, so ioutil.WriteFile writes both files outside the configured log directories to attacker-selected paths writable by the OliveTin process.
causal_research.flaw_origin: The existing API-to-executor path already accepted arbitrary client tracking strings. causal_research.bug_semantics: The unauthenticated GET /images handler accepts request.query.src and passes it to imageProcessor. For any value beginning with http:// or https://, imageProcessor treats it as external, skips all local-path validation, and calls fetch(src) without a destination allowlist or network-address restriction. An attacker can therefore make the EverShop server request attacker-selected external or internal HTTP(S) resources, including link-local metadata services, producing blind SSRF.

causal_research.bug_semantics: The unauthenticated GET /images endpoint accepts an image source and sends the resulting bytes to Sharp. For SVG input, imageProcessor deliberately rasterizes at density 300 with limitInputPixels disabled and performs no structural bound on use-element shadow-tree depth or pattern-tile dimensions. A crafted SVG can therefore make the underlying SVG renderer consume unbounded CPU or memory until the application server, and potentially the host, is denied service.

causal_research.bug_semantics: The public GraphQL Query.order resolver accepts an attacker-controlled order UUID and loads the matching order without authenticating the caller or constraining the query to the caller's customer/session identity. An unauthenticated caller who obtains a valid UUID can therefore traverse the returned Order fields and nested resolvers to read customer email/name, billing and shipping addresses, purchased items, totals, payment state, and shipment data belonging to another customer.

Later commits renamed the argument to uuid, moved the file, and replaced the base select helper, but preserved this authorization omission.

The account_rse_usage WebUI error callbacks passed the raw jqXHR.responseText through string concatenation to jQuery.html(), so the victim's browser parsed payload markup such as an img onerror handler in the Rucio WebUI origin instead of displaying it as text. A crafted link therefore executes script when an authenticated user opens it, exposing the WebUI token/session and permitting actions with the victim's authority.

causal_research.bug_semantics: picklescan disassembles pickle GLOBAL/STACK_GLOBAL references and, in the default scan result, counts a finding only when the referenced module/name matches its hard-coded unsafe-globals blocklist. Through v0.0.34 the blocklist omitted both the serialized global _io.FileIO and urllib.request.urlopen, so a crafted pickle could open an arbitrary local file and pass that file object as the body of an attacker-directed HTTP request without either global being counted as dangerous. A consumer relying on the scan could then deserialize the payload, causing arbitrary file read plus SSRF/data exfiltration.
causal_research.flaw_origin: The initial scanner implementation introduced the incomplete-denylist security model: src/picklescan/scanner.py enumerated selected suspicious globals and scan_pickle_bytes incremented issues_count only for exact blocklist matches, silently leaving unlisted callable globals such as _io.FileIO and urllib.request.urlopen outside the failing result. Later classification of unknown globals as Suspicious did not cure the default-pass behavior because only Dangerous globals incremented issues_count; the vulnerable mechanism therefore originates in the initial scanner commit rather than in a later refactor or blocklist expansion.
causal_research.ai_marker: absent: the BIC commit object names author Matthieu Maitre <mmaitre314@users.noreply.github.com> and committer Matthieu Maitre <mmaitre314@users.noreply.github.com>; its complete message is 'Implement Pickle scanner' with no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, or other trailers, and neither identity is a bot.
causal_research.evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/mmaitre314/picklescan/security/advisories/GHSA-9726-w42j-3qjr specifies affected versions <0.0.35, patched version 0.0.35, and the io.FileIO -> urllib.request.urlopen exfiltration chain. PR https://github.com/mmaitre314/picklescan/pull/55 and release https://github.com/mmaitre314/picklescan/releases/tag/v0.0.35 identify the remediation. In the validated clone, `git log -L 14,24:src/picklescan/scanner.py c1d5abd...` attributes the original suspicious-globals dictionary to c1d5abdcc740e0d08a0d12d015d08e1e6f29a67e, and `git log -L 77,89:src/picklescan/scanner.py c1d5abd...` shows that same new-file commit introduced scan_pickle_bytes with exact blocklist lookup and issues_count increment only on a match. `git cat-file -e 6a76b8c3ac67dc04181e600614ecf2a423cca326:src/picklescan/scanner.py` fails because the path is absent, while `git ls-tree -r --name-only` for that parent shows no src tree, directly verifying parent absence. The BIC's setup.cfg reports version 0.0.1; `git describe --contains --tags` reports c1d5abd... is contained by v0.0.2~12, and `git merge-base c1d5abd... v0.0.34` returns c1d5abd..., proving the mechanism precedes the last vulnerable tag. At v0.0.34, src/picklescan/scanner.py:356-391 maps non-blocklisted globals to Suspicious but increments issues_count only for Dangerous entries, and its unsafe table at lines 110-186 contains neither _io.FileIO nor urllib.request. `git log -S` for both `"_io": {"FileIO"}` and `"urllib.request": "*"` finds only a01c58d5dd7960db557b849817c0ab83ab111ef1. That commit adds both unsafe entries plus regression pickles/tests and changes setup.cfg 0.0.34 -> 0.0.35; v0.0.34 resolves to its immediate parent 323bd004691e442b109b00a1251cd9acc1a4be98, v0.0.35 resolves exactly to a01c58d5dd7960db557b849817c0ab83ab111ef1, and `git describe --contains --tags a01c58d...` returns v0.0.35. Finally, `git cat-file -p c1d5abd...` supplies the human author/committer and trailer-free message quoted in ai_marker.
causal_research.reasoning: The vulnerability is a scanner-detection bypass, not execution performed by picklescan itself: the scanner exposes pickle globals, but its default failing result is driven by a finite dangerous-global dictionary. The advisory's payload serializes io.FileIO as _io.FileIO to open a local file and then invokes urllib.request.urlopen with that file as an iterable request body, so omitting both globals permits the malicious pickle to avoid a Dangerous finding and creates the unsafe trust decision before downstream unpickling. History tracing distinguishes the true origin from later churn: f98f9bd89b16ab1b1b1b6366acddd1b2a4d36fe9 merely renamed _suspicious_globals to _unsafe_globals during PyTorch work, whereas c1d5abdcc740e0d08a0d12d015d08e1e6f29a67e created both the finite blocklist and exact-match reporting logic in one direct, single-parent implementation commit. Its immediate parent has no scanner source at all, so the vulnerable mechanism is directly absent there; no squash/member decomposition or move is needed. The BIC shipped in the initial 0.0.1 code and is ancestral to v0.0.34, while the direct fix a01c58d5dd7960db557b849817c0ab83ab111ef1 is exactly tag v0.0.35 and adds the two missing dangerous globals. AI attribution is restricted to the BIC commit object: it has human author and committer identities, a plain one-line message, and no AI/co-author/generated trailers. Therefore the proven smallest BIC is human-authored and the closed verdict is NOT_AI.

causal_research.bug_semantics: picklescan treated a pickle as infected only when an extracted GLOBAL/STACK_GLOBAL pair matched its finite dangerous-global denylist. A cloudpickle payload could therefore serialize an attacker-controlled function whose bytecode calls getattr(builtins, "eval"): the pickle exposed only cloudpickle reconstruction helpers and types.CodeType, none of which were dangerous entries, so scanning reported no dangerous issue although unpickling reconstructed and invoked executable attacker-controlled code.
causal_research.flaw_origin: The flaw originated in the first scanner implementation: c1d5abdcc740e0d08a0d12d015d08e1e6f29a67e introduced global extraction followed by an exact finite-module/name lookup and incremented issues_count only for matches. That architecture made unlisted callable reconstruction primitives a clean bypass from the scanner's inception; later refactors preserved the mechanism rather than introducing it.

causal_research.bug_semantics: nltk.data.find() validates a still-percent-encoded resource name and later passes it to url2pathname() while constructing a filesystem path. Percent encodings such as %2e%2e therefore survive the raw-string check, decode to .. only at filesystem resolution, escape the configured NLTK data root, and let find()/load() read an arbitrary process-readable file. The pathsec routing present in 3.9.4 only warned because ENFORCE was false, so it did not prevent the read.
causal_research.flaw_origin: Commit 51ceb7517237d78b843a95db56629b11d41ede2b is the smallest introducing change: it imported url2pathname and changed the ordinary-filesystem join from os.path.join(path_, resource_name) to os.path.join(path_, url2pathname(resource_name)). Its immediate parent e8c09039f8d805437a6fea14a3bce619db452eee joined the encoded string unchanged, so the advisory's percent-encoded traversal did not become a filesystem traversal there. Later checks, moves, and security wrappers did not originate that decoding primitive.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An attacker who can add an account identity can POST an identity string containing HTML or JavaScript to /accounts/<account>/identities.
